identity.title: Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit
identity.issuer: Oregon Department of Environmental Quality, Northwest Region

scan.summary: This is an air quality permit issued by Oregon DEQ authorizing Cascade Specialty Chemicals' Portland facility to operate vapor control equipment for chemical storage and repackaging. The permit specifies the equipment allowed, operating conditions, monitoring and reporting requirements, and sets an expiration date. A permit is the agency's own document that has no gaps to fix; what matters is renewing it before expiration and meeting all conditions.
scan.freshness_note: The permit expires November 15, 2026. As of today (September 25, 2026), the permit is 51 days from expiration. A renewal application was due July 18, 2026 (120 days before expiration per condition 1.3). It is now unknown whether that application was submitted; if it was timely and complete, the company may continue operating under current terms while awaiting final action.

conditions.title: Operate sources in compliance with permit and applicable rules
conditions.evidence_expected: Demonstration that operations conform to all specified conditions and Oregon DEQ rules

conditions.title: Permit expires and renewal must be applied for timely
conditions.evidence_expected: Complete renewal application submitted to Oregon DEQ on or before July 18, 2026; proof of submission

conditions.title: Notify Department of ownership change or emission-increasing modifications
conditions.evidence_expected: Written notice to Oregon DEQ at least 60 days in advance of any change in ownership or modifications increasing regulated pollutant emissions

conditions.title: Maintain scrubber pressure drop within specified range
conditions.evidence_expected: Scrubber log with daily pressure drop readings for S-1 (2.0–6.0 inches water column) and S-2 (2.0–6.0 inches water column) when operating

conditions.title: Inspect scrubbers quarterly
conditions.evidence_expected: Scrubber log with dates, inspector name, and corrective actions recorded for each quarterly inspection of recirculation pumps, spray nozzles, packing, and mist eliminators

conditions.title: Replace carbon in adsorption unit C-1 at least annually or upon breakthrough
conditions.evidence_expected: Records of each carbon replacement date; weekly detector-tube checks at C-1 outlet showing no breakthrough, or replacement when breakthrough detected

conditions.title: Limit visible emissions to 20 percent opacity
conditions.evidence_expected: Operational records and observations showing visible emissions do not exceed 20 percent opacity for periods aggregating more than three minutes in any one hour

conditions.title: Submit annual report by February 15
conditions.evidence_expected: Annual report submitted to Oregon DEQ covering previous calendar year, including total throughput by line, scrubber log summaries, carbon replacement dates, and excess emission events

conditions.title: Submit semi-annual monitoring report by July 31
conditions.evidence_expected: Semi-annual report submitted covering January through June

conditions.title: Keep all records for at least five years
conditions.evidence_expected: All required records retained for minimum five years from record date; available for Department inspection on request

conditions.title: Minimize emissions during scrubber malfunction
conditions.evidence_expected: Documentation that reasonable steps were taken to minimize emissions, including stopping repackaging line until scrubber returned to service

conditions.title: Notify Department of permit deviations within 24 hours and report in writing within 15 days
conditions.evidence_expected: Telephone or email notification to Oregon DEQ within 24 hours of discovering any deviation; written report within 15 days describing deviation, cause, duration, and corrective action

conditions.title: Pay annual permit fee by due date
conditions.evidence_expected: Payment receipt or bank record showing annual permit fee paid by the due date shown on Department invoice

facts.quote: Facility address: 4410 NW Front Avenue, Portland, Oregon 97210
facts.affects: Determines jurisdiction (Oregon state law and local rules apply); this is the site where all permitted operations occur.

facts.value: Chemical storage and repackaging with vapor control
facts.quote: Source category: Chemical storage and repackaging with vapor control
facts.affects: Defines the scope of regulated operations; equipment and conditions must match this description.

facts.quote: Packed-bed wet scrubber S-1 serving the acid repackaging line (design flow 4,500 scfm)
facts.affects: Specifies the equipment subject to condition 3.1 (pressure drop monitoring) and condition 3.2 (quarterly inspection); pressure drop must be maintained at 2.0–6.0 inches water column when this line operates.

facts.quote: Packed-bed wet scrubber S-2 serving the caustic repackaging line (design flow 3,000 scfm)
facts.affects: Specifies the equipment subject to condition 3.1 (pressure drop monitoring) and condition 3.2 (quarterly inspection); pressure drop must be maintained at 2.0–6.0 inches water column when this line operates.

facts.value: Four tanks (T-3, T-4, T-5, T-6), each 10,000 gallons, fixed roof, vented to carbon adsorption unit C-1
facts.quote: Solvent storage tanks T-3, T-4, T-5 and T-6 (each 10,000 gallons, fixed roof, vented to carbon adsorption unit C-1)
facts.affects: Specifies the equipment subject to condition 3.3 (carbon replacement at least annually or upon breakthrough detection); total storage capacity is 40,000 gallons.

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence in the permit's identity, issuer, conditions, and deadlines—these are clearly stated by Oregon DEQ. High confidence that the permit is expiring and that a renewal application deadline of July 18, 2026 was set by condition 1.3 (already passed as of today, September 25, 2026). The document was readable in full. The critical unknown is whether a timely and complete renewal application was submitted; if so, the company may continue operating under this permit while awaiting final DEQ action. If not submitted, the company is operating in violation as of September 26, 2026. No other issues with the permit document itself were found—it is the agency's own instrument and contains no gaps against the rules that govern it. The expected_missing list is based on typical holdings of similar companies, not on a checked requirement specific to this company.
